regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

Match visuals to specific narration: On-screen imagery must directly represent spoken technical details like costs, license terms, or user groups, rather than just showing a tool name or logo.
Prioritize genuine tool interfaces and outputs over abstract geometry, generic stock, or stylized illustrations during technical explanations.
Hook within 5 seconds with tool outcomes; avoid date citations, meta-source references, or reading research logs as narration.
Verify all technical claims, software versions, and pricing against sources; prioritize specific visual workflows over generic trending topics.
State catches, license terms, and account restrictions directly in narration without rhetorical questions or filler phrasing.
Preserve genuine evidence and important image details; never fill gaps with unrelated stock, background-only frames, or tiny repeated photos.
Adapt pacing to the format: use high-frequency motif changes for Shorts without imposing that speed on purposeful long-video demonstrations.
Position mandatory CTAs immediately after the first visual payoff in Shorts or between 45 and 80 seconds in long videos.
Maintain seamless loop transitions from the ending back to the hook while preserving the demonstrated tool utility.
Phrase technical findings as natural spoken narration; do not read internal database logs, check-dates, or raw research notes.
Treat review feedback as conditional data to refine visual alignment; do not overgeneralize specific defects or assume unobserved viewer causes.

skript.beschreibung: The youtube-agent-skill repo offers eleven Claude skills under an MIT license, with no signup or API key. They write advice and drafts, and nothing publishes until you upload.

belege.name: youtube-agent-skill README (GitHub, Jakeschincariol)
belege.text: Official repo README (fetched 2026-11-23). Eleven Claude skills for a YouTube channel, free, MIT license, no signup, no API key. /yt-script writes five hooks from 21 hook formulas, scores them, then the script; /yt-package lints title and thumbnail as one pairing; /yt-edit turns a transcript into an edit decision list; /yt-comment triages comments; /yt-plan plans a week; /yt-viral ranks videos in a niche by how far each beat its own channel median; /yt-retention reads the YouTube Studio audience-retention export and reports hook leak (loss in the first 30 seconds), cliffs (steep drops) and slide; /yt-shorts finds Shorts inside a long video; /yt-seo; /yt-chapters; /yt-audit ends in one fix. Six small Python tools without dependencies. Install by pasting the GitHub link into Claude or copying the skill folders. The README stresses: nothing gets published until you do it - the skills write, you upload. Repo history: a single commit dated 2026-09-16.

belege.name: youtube-agent-skill hooks.json (21 hook formulas)
belege.text: Repo file (fetched 2026-11-23). Defines 21 hook formulas (for example The Statistic, The Mistake, Contrarian Flip, The Reveal, The Clock, I Tried It, The Question, Before and After, The Warning, The List, The Comparison, The Deadline, The Direct Address), each with shape, example and failure mode. Rules listed: confirm the title in the first sentence; one idea per hook; specific beats big; show the promised artifact inside 20 seconds; never open with who you are. The repo itself notes that matching a title to a formula is a judgement about the title, not a claim about why the video worked.

belege.name: youtube-agent-skill yt-retention SKILL.md
belege.text: Repo file (fetched 2026-11-23). The retention skill reads the audience-retention CSV you download yourself in YouTube Studio (Analytics, Engagement, audience-retention chart, download). It reports hook leak (under 25 percent lost in the first 30 seconds is called healthy), cliffs (single steep drops, with the words spoken there if a transcript is given) and slide (steady loss across the middle). Nothing is published by the skill.
